transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Well, um, it's kind of a lot of little things building up, to be honest. I work as a secretary, so my whole day is supposed to be about keeping things on track, but lately I just... well, what finally made me actually reach out and ask for help is that I just keep forgetting all these little things that I normally handle just fine. It's really starting to drive me crazy. 

Like, at work, I'll completely forget to return phone calls. I'll get the message, and then it just completely leaves my brain the second I turn around. Or, in my personal life, like the other day I had this registration form I needed to turn in. I had it all filled out and ready to go, and I just... didn't. I completely forgot about it until it was past the deadline. 

And errands! Errands are just a nightmare right now. I can't tell you how many times I've told myself I need to stop for an errand on the way home from work—like just grabbing something from the store or picking up dry cleaning—and I will literally drive the entire way home, pull into my driveway, put the car in park, and realize I drove right past the place and completely forgot to stop. It's just these everyday, basic things, and I don't understand why I can't seem to remember them. It's really making me feel like I'm dropping the ball on my own life, you know?
Can you tell me how you’ve been feeling emotionally lately? Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, no, it's not really like that. I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down in the dumps. I mean, my mood is actually pretty okay most of the time! I still love doing all the things I usually do. Like, I still look forward to the weekends, I still enjoy going out or just, you know, relaxing and watching my favorite shows in the evening. I haven't lost interest in any of that at all. 

It's really more just... well, it's frustration, honestly. Just pure exasperation with myself. Because I'll be having a perfectly good day, feeling totally fine, maybe even in a really great mood, and then I'll realize I forgot to make that phone call at work, or I'll pull into the driveway and realize I drove right past the dry cleaners again. And in that moment, yeah, I get really mad at myself. I'll think, "Ugh, why are you like this? Why can't you just remember one simple thing?" 

So it's more like I'm just incredibly annoyed. But it doesn't linger into this big, dark cloud or anything like that. I don't feel like giving up, and I definitely don't feel hopeless about my life in general. I just want to fix this one specific thing that's driving me up the wall, because otherwise, emotionally, I feel like I'm doing alright. It's just the constant dropping the ball on these little tasks that really gets under my skin and makes me feel flustered. But no, not depressed or losing interest in things, definitely not.
Have you noticed these kinds of forgetful or distracted moments happening in other areas of your life, like in conversations, while reading, or during hobbies?

Oh, definitely. It's not just the errands or the forms, it's really... well, especially at the office. You know how offices are, right? We have our desks set up pretty close together, and it's just a nightmare for my concentration lately. I'll be right in the middle of typing up an email or entering some data—something I really need to get done for my boss—and literally just one phone ringing at the desk across from me is enough to completely derail my train of thought. And it doesn't even have to be my phone! I'll just hear it ring and suddenly I've lost my place. 

Or, if I hear people talking nearby, like if two of my coworkers are just chatting over by the copier or the break area, I suddenly can't focus on my screen at all. I start tuning into their conversation without even meaning to, you know? Like, my brain just latches onto what they're saying about their weekend, and before I know it, my hands have stopped typing entirely and I'm just sitting there listening, completely forgetting the email I was halfway through. 

But it's not even just external stuff, which is the craziest part! Sometimes it's just my own brain doing it to me. I'll be sitting there working, totally quiet, nobody is talking, no phones are ringing, and then just a completely random thought about something at home will pop into my head. Like, I'll suddenly wonder if I remembered to take the chicken out of the freezer to thaw, or I'll start thinking about whether I need to buy more laundry detergent, and boom—I'm completely pulled off what I was working on. I'll just sit there staring at the computer screen, totally lost in thought about my house, and then five minutes later I have to shake myself out of it and try to figure out where I even was in my work. 

And you mentioned reading! It happens when I try to read a book at home, too. I used to love reading, but now I'll read the same page three times because I started thinking about that chicken in the freezer again. It's just so frustrating because I really do want to stay on task, but every little noise or random thought just yanks my attention right away from whatever is right in front of me.
Have you noticed yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated, especially in situations where you’re expected to remain still or focused for a while?

Oh, well, sitting still... I mean, I don't feel like I need to get up and run laps around the building or anything, but I definitely do get a little... I don't know, squirmy? Especially when I'm stuck somewhere for a long time. 

Like, occasionally I have to take these longer classes for work, you know, like software training or continuing education seminars, and oh my gosh, those are just so hard to sit through. I’ll be sitting there in those terrible conference room chairs—the ones that have absolutely no lower back support whatsoever—and I am just constantly shifting around in the chair. I try so hard to just sit still and pay attention to the instructor, because I really do want to learn the material and get something out of it, but I’ll catch myself clicking my pen over and over. Like, click, click, click. And I honestly don't even realize I'm doing it until I catch someone at the next table glancing over at me! 

Or, um, if I'm not doing that, I'll be bouncing my foot under the table, just tapping my heel up and down a mile a minute. It’s like my body just has this tiny bit of extra energy that needs to get out, even though I’m actively telling myself, "Okay, sit perfectly still, just focus." But yeah, in those longer classes especially, I’m just always adjusting my posture, crossing and uncrossing my legs, bouncing my foot, messing with my pen... it’s just really hard to stay completely frozen in one spot for that long, you know? I just can't seem to stay totally still, no matter how much I'm trying to just be a good listener.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with attention and staying still? Were you like this even as a child, or is this something that's developed more recently in your life?

Oh my gosh, no, it’s definitely not a new thing at all. Honestly, if I really sit back and think about it... I’ve been like this for as long as I can remember. Like, even way back in elementary school, I was absolutely *that* kid. You know the one. I was the kid who was always forgetting her permission slips for field trips. It was a whole ordeal every single time! The teacher would hand them out, I’d shove the paper into my backpack, and then... poof, it was just completely gone from my brain until the morning of the trip when everyone else was lining up. 

And my backpack, oh, it was just a complete black hole of crumpled papers and broken pencils. I would lose my actual homework in there all the time! I’d sit at the kitchen table, do the math worksheet, put it in the bag, and then the next day I’d be digging around frantically while the teacher was collecting them, and I just couldn't find it buried under all the mess. It was so embarrassing. 

And big assignments? Forget about it. If we had a science fair or a diorama or something, I was completely lost. I literally needed my mother or my teacher to remind me step by step just to finish projects. Like, my mom would have to sit there at the table with me and say, "Okay, first we read the chapter. Good. Now we write the first paragraph. Okay, now we cut the paper." If they didn't break it down into these tiny little steps and constantly remind me what I was supposed to be doing next, I would just drift off. I'd start doodling on the folder or looking out the window, and the project would just never get done. 

So my mom was constantly having to intervene and manage my time for me. It’s actually kind of ironic when you think about it, because now I do administrative work for a living, organizing other people's schedules, but back then—and honestly, even now with my own personal stuff—it's just always been this exact same struggle. So yeah, definitely not a recent development. It's really been the story of my life since I was a little girl!
